rule: The headline carries the ad. It must stop the scroll and send the eye to the product with curiosity. A good headline does not save a weak image either.
quote: extremely crucial critical

rule: Generic, average or pointless headlines and boring concepts are a Pass. Prefer an oddly specific true detail or a buyer's own words, used word for word.
quote: boring, non-creative concepts

rule: Calm ads win: one focal product, little to look at.
quote: because they weren't chaotic or busy like B39

rule: A clever object that IS the headline's idea is the best kind of ad (butter on toast, a zested lemon, an empty snail shell for 'The snail had a good run.').
quote: A clever object that IS the headline's idea

rule: Add a short, true supporting line under the headline when the product page backs it. Without it the ad feels incomplete.
quote: A true supporting tagline under the headline

rule: Show a real serving only when it shows what the pack hides (the tart inside the tin, the layers) or the size of a food sold by weight.
quote: A real serving only when it shows what the pack hides

rule: Every prop, sticker, tagline and callout must add meaning. One filler prop (a spare bowl, spoon, plate, blanket, saucer, ice tray, glass of water) turns a good ad into a reject. An upturned bowl reads unlucky.
quote: Props that add no meaning

rule: Props match the brand's level (a fine Chinese teacup for a heritage brand), never cheap props (tote, foil, plastic bottle).
quote: Props that match the brand's level

rule: No AI slop: no drip on a cup, no painted prepared food, no doubled or flat-printed product, no garbled letters.
quote: very ai slop looking less premium

rule: A wrong or garbled logo, or a logo outside the safe zone, rejects the ad by itself. Draw the real logo file in code, never paint it.
quote: A wrong or garbled logo, or a logo outside the safe zone: that alone rejects the ad

rule: Food must look like the real product's own food, from its real photo, and look appetising. Painted food, glossy round kernels and plastic-looking colour are rejected.
quote: food seems ai slop not true to actual real life product

rule: Do not push food colour past the real photo: a richer caramel colour looked fake and plastic.
quote: simply fake looking plastic looking

rule: The product's container keeps its real shape, height, width and camera angle. Build it from the real packshot pixels, never from a model redraw.
quote: the product's container doesn't match real life too, the dimensions height and width

rule: In a row of identical packs the food must differ pack to pack. No pattern may be visible to the eye.
quote: there can be no patterns Discernible decipherable from a human eye

rule: A pasted product must sit in the scene: the same light, shadow and blending as the room. It must not look pasted in.
quote: it looks pasted in

rule: The brand logo must be big enough to read at a glance, with breathing room above it.
source: marks.md, W46c v2 and v3 (the numbers for width and top are in creative-playbook §7.4 Logo room)
quote: the wongi logo branding needs to be big enough

rule: A moment in the copy must be true to Singapore life. Do not invent habits.
quote: Baking lapis this CNY? Not again.

rule: Never name or hint at an ethnicity, race or religion, or a negative association. Reject on sight.
quote: really really bad headline, sounds racist

rule: Filler stickers and taglines are a Pass: shelf life, thin review counts, a rating line that adds nothing, a useless discount sticker. Keep taglines short and useful.
quote: useless 15% off tagline sticker

rule: A top-of-funnel ad carries no offer sticker.
quote: An offer sticker on a ToF ad

rule: A bottom-of-funnel ad needs a real reason to buy now and a correct price.
quote: A BoF ad with no reason to buy now

rule: The flavour named in the headline is the flavour in the picture.
quote: A headline flavour that is not the slice in front

rule: No unneeded hands, no wrong scale and no busy layouts.
quote: Unneeded hands, wrong scale, cheap props
